stem:
**Statements:**

All biscuits are chocolates.

Some chocolates are breads.

All breads are pastries.

**Conclusions**

I. Some biscuits are pastries.

II. Some pastries are chocolates.
solution: Some chocolates are breads and all breads are pastries, so some chocolates are pastries, i.e. some pastries are chocolates: II follows. There is no definite link between biscuits and breads/pastries, so I does not follow.

stem:
**Statements:**

Some pots are buckets.

Some buckets are bags.

Some bags are purses.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some purses are buckets.

II. Some bags are pots.
solution: Two particular ("some") premises give no definite conclusion, so neither I nor II follows.

stem: Find the missing number in the following series: 27, 29, 33, ?, 57
A family has a man, his wife, their four sons and their wives. The family of every son also have 3 sons and one daughter. Find out the total number of male members in the family.

solution: In figures A, B and D the second letter is the mirror image (lateral inversion) of the first; in figure C the second letter is the water image (inverted) of T. So C is the odd one out.

stem: Choose the mirror image for the following figure when the mirror is kept at the MN line.
solution: With a vertical mirror MN, left and right are interchanged while top and bottom stay the same; the shaded small square moves to the left side. Figure A matches.

stem: If the angle made by the tangent at the point $(x_0, y_0)$ on the curve $x = 12(t + \sin t\cos t)$, $y = 12(1 + \sin t)^2$, $0 < t < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, with the positive x-axis is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$, then $y_0$ is equal to
solution:
$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 12(1 + \cos 2t) = 24\cos^2 t$, $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 24(1 + \sin t)\cos t$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 + \sin t}{\cos t} = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{t}{2}\right) = \tan\dfrac{\pi}{3} \Rightarrow t = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$y_0 = 12\left(1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = 27$

stem: The integral $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{x^2(x\sec^2 x + \tan x)}{(x\tan x + 1)^2}\,dx$ is equal to
solution:
Since $\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\tan x + 1) = x\sec^2 x + \tan x$, integrate by parts with $u = x^2$:

$I = -\dfrac{x^2}{x\tan x + 1} + \displaystyle\int \dfrac{2x}{x\tan x + 1}dx = -\dfrac{x^2}{x\tan x + 1} + \displaystyle\int \dfrac{2x\cos x}{x\sin x + \cos x}dx$

$= -\dfrac{x^2}{x\tan x + 1} + 2\log_e|x\sin x + \cos x| + c$
